title: Energy Attacks in War on Iran Could Turn Economic Shock Into Long-Term Damage
partialText: A new phase targeting oil and gas infrastructure in the Persian Gulf threatens to hurt businesses and customers around the world for months or even years.

title: Oil Prices Tumble and Stocks Rise as Trump Backs Off Threats to Iran Infrastructure
partialText: Investors braced for a fourth week of market turmoil caused by the war in the Middle East

title: Air Traffic Audio Appears to Show Tower Was Dealing With Incident Before Crash
partialText: Several minutes after the collision, a controller told the pilot of a Frontier jet that “we were dealing with an emergency earlier,” according to audio reviewed by The New York Times.

title: Deadly Plane Crash at LaGuardia Airport: What We Know
partialText: Two pilots were killed and dozens of others were injured when a regional jet collided with a fire truck on the runway.

title: When Voters Worry About ‘Affordability,’ Many Point to Health Care
partialText: Democrats have had limited political success running on the Affordable Care Act, even with its relative popularity. Now President Trump’s health care cuts may have given the issue new resonance.

title: In California, a Republican Sheriff Seizes Ballots, Prompting Concerns
partialText: Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco, a candidate for governor, recently took possession of more than 650,000 ballots as part of a fraud probe. Election officials say his investigation is baseless.

title: How Obama’s Strategist Discouraged Biden From Running in 2016
partialText: In a new set of oral histories, David Plouffe, President Barack Obama’s political adviser, described how he urged Vice President Joseph R. Biden Jr. not to challenge Hillary Clinton for the nomination.

title: Trump Is Digging Up Washington. Can Lawsuits Stop the Bulldozers?
partialText: As the president develops plans to fundamentally alter the White House, the Kennedy Center and other sites, federal lawsuits are beginning to catch up.

title: Takeaways From The Times’s Inside Look at the C.D.C.
partialText: Many current and former employees say the actions of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. are undermining the agency’s role in safeguarding public health.

title: A Professional’s Guide to Spring Cleaning Your Life
partialText: Tackle clutter, let go of sentimental objects and create a home that reflects who you are now.

title: Born Abroad and Fearful of ICE, Adoptees Try to Prove They Belong
partialText: Up to 200,000 people adopted as children from abroad are vulnerable to deportation by an administration searching for problems with their citizenship.

title: Immigrant Detentions and Deportations Leave Pets Behind
partialText: As immigrant detentions and self-deportations soar, animal welfare groups in cities like New Orleans scramble to feed, foster and re-home the pets left behind.

title: How Epstein Helped Solve a Billionaire’s Problems With Women
partialText: The Wall Street titan Leon Black paid Jeffrey Epstein $170 million for what he said was tax and estate work. But his services went beyond that.

title: What’s It Like to Be Back in Print After 20 Years? A Bit Odd.
partialText: Nancy Lemann published her first novel at 28. Then came “the doom.” Now she’s back in the spotlight, and not exactly comfortable with it.

title: Canada’s Military Wants to Prove It Can Defend the High Arctic
partialText: Canadian soldiers transported M777 howitzers to the High Arctic to show their ability to fight in an increasingly contested part of the world. It did not go as planned.

title: Jewish and Muslim People Face a Wave of Hate. Can Schools Turn the Tide?
partialText: New York City is rolling out lessons on Jewish and Muslim American history. Too often, some leaders say, what students know comes from TikTok and social media.

title: London Arson Attack on Jewish Ambulance Service Investigated as Hate Crime, Police Say
partialText: The city’s main police force said it was investigating fires that struck four ambulances as an antisemitic hate crime.

title: Review: On ‘Arirang,’ BTS Is Too Big to Fail. But Not Too Big to Succeed.
partialText: The K-pop superstars’ new album, “Arirang,” comes with huge commercial expectations. The group made room for artistic experimentation, too.

title: Why the BTS Comeback Concert Was a ‘Disaster’ for Some Businesses
partialText: The turnout for the K-pop titans’ show was much lower than projected by officials, hitting the bottom line of some restaurants. Shares in the group’s management company also fell.

title: We Shouldn’t Want a World Run by Prediction Markets
partialText: Prediction markets teach us to look at the future as gamblers, rather than as citizens.

title: Chuck Schumer: What the SAVE Act Would Really Do
partialText: Republicans want to pretend the SAVE Act is a voter ID bill.

title: Death by Paper
partialText: We examine a new innovation in drug smuggling.

title: N.Y.U. Professors Go on Strike, Seeking Better Pay and Job Protections
partialText: About 950 full-time faculty members who are not on the tenure track walked out. The university told students that classes would continue.

title: Diabetes, Overlooked and Unchecked, Poses New Risks in Africa
partialText: As deaths from diabetes start to rival those from infectious threats like malaria, a new form of the condition linked to malnutrition is surfacing in patients who can afford neither screening nor care.

title: A Choice of Deadly Drones Is Only a Few Clicks Away for Ukrainian Troops
partialText: Ukraine has created online marketplaces to let units select their own drones, a break from generations of standardized and centralized weapons procurement.
